title: opum-lore pane: generation-token the tick guard so a stale tick cannot clear a successor session's tickInFlight (LCLI-709 follow-up)
description:
Filed by lore-cli's session from LCLI-709's round-1 review, citing LCLI-709 and DEC-172 (4bi)(a).

LCLI-709 generation-tokened the REFRESH guard at session.end (a refresh still unwinding under an older generation leaves the successor session's flags alone). The TICK guard `tickInFlight` in hooks/register.tsx is still cleared at session.end and is NEVER compared against the generation, so a stale tick's `finally` can clear a successor session's `tickInFlight` — the SAME clobber shape LCLI-709 fixed for the refresh guard. LCLI-709's reviewer found it by reading the new comment's claim ("Both guards carry a session GENERATION") against the mechanism, where only the refresh guard actually carried one.

The overlap is BOUNDED, and that bound is why this is LOW: a stacked tick's `refresh($)` still coalesces on `refreshInFlight`, so at most an extra `countUncommitted` (one `git status`) can overlap. No test exercises the tick path across session.end today.

Scope: generation-token `tickInFlight` the way LCLI-709 did `refreshInFlight`/`refreshQueued`, so a stale tick's cleanup is inert under an older generation. Once that holds, the comment "Both guards carry a session GENERATION" becomes true. If a fix is ever dropped instead, the acceptance is to NARROW that comment to the refresh guard alone. Not the refresh guard (already done), and not a redesign of the coalescing behaviour.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The tick guard `tickInFlight` is generation-tokened like the refresh guard: a tick still running when session.end fires cannot clear a successor session's `tickInFlight` (its cleanup is inert under an older generation).
Proved both ways with a test that drives a tick across session.end: RED without the token, GREEN with it, both runs MEASURED and recorded on the task.
The comment "Both guards carry a session GENERATION" in hooks/register.tsx is true once the token holds; if a fix is ever dropped instead, that comment is narrowed to the refresh guard alone.

implementationNotes:
Implemented LCLI-710 (AC1, per opum-doc's preference over the AC3 fallback of narrowing the comment). `hooks/register.tsx`: the tick callback now captures `sessionGeneration` when it starts and clears `tickInFlight` in its `finally` ONLY when that generation still matches — reusing LCLI-709's SINGLE generation mechanism, not a second one. So a tick that outlived `session.end` can no longer clear the successor session's `tickInFlight` (the same clobber shape LCLI-709 fixed for the refresh guard). With that in place the comment "Both guards carry a session GENERATION" is now TRUE, which is how AC3 is met.

Proof both ways (AC2), MEASURED and recorded, not predicted:
- RED without the token: with the tick's `finally` reverted to an unconditional `tickInFlight = false` (mutation applied and run), the new test "a tick that outlives session.end cannot clear the successor session's tickInFlight (LCLI-710)" FAILS — measured 71 tests / 1 fail, and the failing test is exactly that one.
- GREEN with it: reverted to the committed form, the mod suite is 71 pass / 0 fail (mod typecheck clean).

The test drives a real tick across a session boundary: tick #1 runs in session A and is held mid-body; `session.end` bumps the generation and cancels the clock; a SECOND `session.start` registers a fresh clock and tick #2 runs there, also held; then tick #1 is released and a further tick fires. With the token that third tick is SKIPPED; without it, tick #1's unwind cleared `tickInFlight` and the third tick starts a second concurrent tick. A control asserts tick #1's unwind actually landed its `countUncommitted` (so a green is not a run in which no tick happened).

Bounded, as recorded: a stacked tick's `refresh($)` still coalesces on `refreshInFlight`, so at most an extra `countUncommitted` (one `git status`) can overlap.

Gates: `bun run test:mod` 71 pass / 0 fail (mod typecheck clean); `bun test` 5008 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail; `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck` and `bun run lore check` (exit 0) green.
finalSummary: LCLI-710 (AC1, per opum-doc): the tick guard tickInFlight is generation-tokened like the refresh guard, reusing LCLI-709's SINGLE sessionGeneration (no second mechanism), so a tick that outlived session.end cannot clear the successor session's tickInFlight. With that, the comment "Both guards carry a session GENERATION" is TRUE, which is how AC3 is met. Proved BOTH ways with a test that drives a tick across session.end: RED without the token (71 tests / 1 fail, the failing test exactly this one, measured), GREEN with it (71 pass / 0 fail). The overlap stays bounded — a stacked tick's refresh still coalesces on refreshInFlight, so at most an extra countUncommitted (one git status) can overlap. Gates: test:mod 71/0 (mod typecheck clean), bun test 5008 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail, lint, typecheck, lore check exit 0. Delivered under opum-control job-18tevfl.
